column1: # CI lanes: the one assignment of every scripts/ci-gates.tsv gate to the CI
# job that proves it on each host (#7767 slice 2, council decision D-C42).
# scripts/ci-lane.sh reads this file; .github/workflows/ci.yml lists only the
# lane names. Each lane job runs scripts/ci-verify.sh --gates with the gates it
# owns (with their needs closure and its own bootstrap) and seals a receipt in
# its compiler stage envelope. The per-host aggregator jobs, which keep the
# required-check names, pass only when every lane succeeded and the receipts
# prove each host gate passed in its owning lane.
# id: every gate of scripts/ci-gates.tsv, exactly once.
# linux, windows: - when the gate does not run on that host, otherwise
# OWNER[+LANE...]. OWNER is the lane whose job proves the gate; each further
# LANE also runs it only because gates it owns need it, and every such
# duplicate must be declared here. A lane is HOST-N, at most two per host,
# and its job is named "CI lane HOST-N". An unassigned, doubly assigned,
# unknown or undeclared gate fails every lane and aggregator.
# Lane linux-1 isolates build-invariance with its opt2-CLI consumer, so CI
# runs it with three pool workers; the Windows lanes come from the D-C42
